title: AHEAD-Quant: headwise activation-aware INT8 calibration pipeline and lightweight runtime rescale plugin
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement AHEAD-Quant (Attention Head-Aware Dynamic quantization), a calibration and runtime flow that produces head-wise INT8 scale profiles and a tiny runtime rescale plugin so we can safely quantize MHA-heavy models with minimal accuracy regression. This is an alternative/complimentary approach to per-layer smoothquant: instead of only cross-tensor scaling we identify per-attention-head activation sensitivity and emit a compact head-scale map applied as a single fused rescale before quantized matmuls at runtime.

Scope:
- Offline calibration harness that profiles representative prompts to compute per-head activation statistics (min/max, histograms, KL divergence to FP32).
- Head-sensitivity ranking that tags heads as low/medium/high sensitivity and chooses per-head scale or falls back to FP16 for highest-sensitivity heads.
- Exportable quant profile format (compact JSON) that runtime can consume; profile includes layer path, head index, scale factor, and confidence score.
- Lightweight runtime plugin (C++ + CUDA) that applies a fused per-head rescale step inside the attention kernel with fallbacks to existing kernels when headwise scaling is unsupported on a device. Plugin should be <2KB extra per-layer metadata and add <=2% token latency for 1kB prompt sizes.
- Validation harness (perplexity, top-k overlap, ROUGE/BLEU on generation prompts and targeted regression tests) and automatic regression gating for rollouts.

Deliverables:
1) calibration tool (Python) that consumes a prompt corpus, runs representative batches through the FP32/FP16 model, produces headwise scales and sensitivity scores, and writes a compact quant profile.
2) runtime rescales plugin + kernel hook integrated into runtime-1.22. The plugin must detect device capability at load time and either register fused kernel or fall back to per-tensor rescale + existing matmul.
3) accuracy validation suite and CI job that compares baseline FP16/FP32 outputs vs INT8 with AHEAD profile across a curated prompt set (LLM-perf subset + internal generation prompts).
4) Migration doc + rollout guide for Dedicated/Private customers and an SDK example in Python.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Median generation perplexity delta <= 1% for base Llama-like models and <= 2% for instruction-tuned models on our validation set.
- Token latency overhead <= 2% p50 on a c5r-ish baseline for typical short-turn prompts.
- Profile size <= 2KB per 12-layer transformer block (scales only).
- CI regression gate fails if any prompt exceeds a 5% metric regression without opt-out.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Per-head scaling reduces blunt layer-wide distortion but increases profile complexity. We accept a small increase in metadata size to avoid failing rare but high-impact heads.
- Avoid per-token dynamic re-scaling (which would be expensive); use head-level static scales derived from representative corpus. For latency-sensitive customers we provide a mixed strategy (hot heads FP16/FP32, others INT8).
- Kernel integration strategy: prefer a fused pre-attention rescale that multiplies the value tensor V by head-scale factors broadcasted across sequence dim. If fused kernel unsupported, fall back to fast elementwise CUDA kernel followed by standard quantized matmul.

Security & compliance: profiles contain no customer data — all calibration should be run on anonymized representative prompts or customer-provided prompts processed in customer VPC for Private deployments. Documented guidance for on-prem calibration is required.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: scoping meeting with Tomás (runtime), Morgan (API), and Leah (QA). Agreed on headwise profile format and storage as sidecar JSON to saved model.

2025-02-18 - Prototype calibration run: initial head histograms show a long-tail of 5-8 heads with high activation variance in gpt-small-variant. Preliminary per-head scales reduced L2 activation drift vs per-layer scaling.
2025-02-21 - Engineering spike: Wei implemented a reference Python pass that computes KL-based sensitivity; results pushed to internal repo (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ahead-quant, PR #12).

2025-02-25 - Kernel feasibility: Tomás produced microbenchmarks for fused rescale + matmul on A100 and T4; fused approach adds ~1.1% p50 latency on 1024 context. Decision: proceed with fused kernel and elementwise fallback.
2025-02-28 - QA: Morgan added 120-shot generation suite for regression testing. Early INT8 with headwise rescales matched FP16 perplexity within 0.9% on the LLM-perf subset.
2025-03-03 - PR opened: runtime integration (WIP) - github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3247. Needs API review for profile loading and security sign-off for profile parsing code.
2025-03-04 - Blocker found: Dedicated cluster packaging needs the fused kernel static linking to play nicely with older CUDA on some customer infra. Tomás to prototype lazy-JIT kernel fallback.
Next: complete CI job, PR review, add rollout doc, and schedule canary on dedicated cluster (small customer cohort).
